articles.topic: CCPC gift-voucher enforcement warning and practical consumer rights
articles.distinct_thesis: The new enforcement warning is converted into a consumer decision guide: which vouchers receive the five-year protection, what happens after a partial spend, which products are excluded and how to document and report a refusal.

claim_checks.claim: CCPC officers used consumer reports to identify traders whose vouchers may not comply, wrote to traders and said further enforcement may follow.
claim_checks.basis: CCPC press release dated 20 November 2026; the article does not infer how many businesses were contacted or that every recipient breached the law.

claim_checks.claim: Covered vouchers must last at least five years where an expiry applies, cannot be limited in number per transaction and allow a balance above €1 to be returned in an approved form.
claim_checks.basis: CCPC statutory guidance and Consumer Protection (Gift Vouchers) Act 2019; exclusions and 2 December 2019 start date are stated.

claim_checks.claim: A €100 voucher used for a €63 purchase leaves €37.

articles.topic: Bank of Ireland Youth Mind and Money 2026 saving and investment-confidence gap
articles.distinct_thesis: The article measures the gap between saving behaviour, investment interest and confidence, then separates cash and investment jobs while explicitly disclosing the commissioned survey's size, age range, timing and missing cross-tabulation limits.

claim_checks.claim: 73% said they saved regularly, 56% were interested in investing and 30% felt confident they understood investment products.
claim_checks.basis: Bank of Ireland release dated 20 November 2026 about Ipsos B&A research among 526 people aged 13-30; described as survey results rather than population facts.

claim_checks.claim: Regular saving rose 9 percentage points from 64% to 73%, a relative increase of approximately 14.1%; investment interest exceeded confidence by 26 points.
Crypto participation fell from 36% to 16% in the published summary.
claim_checks.basis: Bank release; article states that the denominator is not fully explained and does not infer direct asset switching or longitudinal behaviour.

articles.topic: Confirmed 2027/28 Irish school-transport charges and family cost impact
articles.distinct_thesis: The article distinguishes the current official fee page from reported 2027/28 charges, calculates five household cases, narrows the exemption language to the actual eligibility tests and states which next-year application details are not yet published.

claim_checks.claim: For 2027/28, primary remains €100 with a €220 primary cap; post-primary becomes €350 with a €650 overall family cap.
claim_checks.basis: Written parliamentary response from the Minister of State reproduced by original reporting on 20 November and corroborated by RTÉ's Department and Tánaiste reporting. The live Department page still shows 2026/27 terms, which the article distinguishes.

claim_checks.claim: Two post-primary pupils cost €200 in 2026/27 and €650 under the announced 2027/28 family cap, an increase of €450.
Eligible medical-card holders and children approved for specialised transport remain exempt.
claim_checks.basis: Current Department and Bus Éireann terms plus 20 November official statements reported by RTÉ; article does not broaden this to every means-tested family.
